newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says concerned about Japan trade surplus.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says concerned about Japan trade surplus.

text.p: President Clinton said Thursday he was concerned about Japan's large trade surplus with the United States but said he understood that Japan was taking steps to boost domestic economic demand.

In a White House interview with Japan's Fuji television network just before he was to leave for the Group of Seven summit in Denver, Colorado, Clinton also said that exchange rates should not be used as a way to correct trade imbalances.
He said the dollar had been strong because of the strength of the U.S. economy.
The widening trade gap between the United States and Japan has again become a key dispute between the two countries.
Earlier on Thursday, the U.S. Commerce Department said that the U.S. deficit with Japan grew by 5.1 percent to $4.84 billion in April.
On Wednesday, Japan said that its merchandise trade surplus with the United States, surged 93 percent in May from a year earlier to 322.87 billion yen ($2.85 billion).
In the area of security ties, Clinton said that the U.S.-Japan security agreement is crucial to relations between the two countries.
He also said that North Korea, which has said it is ready for a "final battle" with South Korea and the United States, poses no immediate security threat.
But he noted that the Stalinist state, in the middle of a serious food shortage, has substantial military power.

He also said that he hopes Japan and Russia will work out a dispute over isolated islands claimed by both countries. The dispute has stopped the two countries from signing a formal pact to end World War Two.
Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said in Tokyo he will press Russian President Boris Yeltsin to resolve the dispute.
He also said that he would like to discuss the June 30 handover of Hong Kong to China and said that he hopes China will respect human rights after taking control of the British territory.
He said that it is important for China to continue its economic reforms and that as its economic power grows, the G7 will have to consider its membership.
But he said that the G7 first needs to consider what terms under which China could join the exclusive group.
Clinton's remarks were dubbed into Japanese by Fuji TV for the broadcast, and Reuters translated them back into English.
